scenes.title: Only the Neighbour Next Door
scenes.summary: The Tuesday-night knock turns out to be a neighbour returning a misdelivered city envelope confirming Wednesday's three-o'clock visit.
scenes.intro: At ten o'clock Tuesday night at {SHOW}, {F1}, {M1}, and {M2} hurry to the front door expecting an early city inspector—and find their next-door neighbour smiling on the step instead. Listen first.
story: Phew! My heart nearly jumped over the courtyard tree!
It was only the bookshop owner next door bringing our mail!
Read the stamped city envelope she handed you, {F1}.
'Public Heritage Café Review — Wednesday, three o'clock sharp.'
Thank goodness—not tonight! Read the checklist inside, {F1}!
Item one: clear street sign and open courtyard access for neighbours.
Item two: bright, safe indoor seating with fresh hot tea and food.
Twelve chairs, clean windows, new copper wire—and two mystery white jars!
Label those jars right now before anyone sleeps, {F1}.
Left spoon... sweet! Right spoon... salty as the sea! Big red labels on both!
Crisis averted! Everyone to bed—six o'clock comes fast!
scenes.outro: Sugar and salt are clearly labelled in red, the checklist is clear, and Wednesday morning's six-o'clock kitchen shift awaits. See you next time.

scenes.title: General in an Apron
scenes.summary: At 6:00 AM Wednesday, F2 sits with her ankle on pillows directing M4's bread kneading and F1's lemon curd like a cheerful general.
scenes.intro: At six o'clock Wednesday morning, warm light fills the kitchen where {F2} sits comfortably with her ankle propped on two pillows, tapping a wooden spoon like a conductor's baton for {M4} and {F1}. Let's listen in first.
story: Push with the heel of your hand, {M4}, fold once, quarter turn, push again!
Yes, Chef! How does the dough look now?
Smooth, soft, and springing right back—into the warm bowl under a damp cloth!
Four egg yolks, fresh lemon juice, and three spoons from the SUGAR jar, {F2}!
Keep whisking over gentle heat, {F1}—never let the bottom boil!
How is your ankle feeling this morning, {F2}?
Honestly? Half the swelling is gone already because you two kept me off my feet!
Look how thick and glossy the yellow lemon curd just turned!
Off the flame immediately! Stir in one cold cube of unsalted butter!
Smell that bright lemon steam filling the whole ground floor!
Twenty crisp almond tart shells ready on the cooling tray!
Not bad at all, apprentices—my bakery is in safe hands!
scenes.outro: Under Chef {F2}'s watchful eye, the bread dough rises and glossy lemon curd fills twenty golden tarts. See you next time.

scenes.title: Carrots by the Millimetre
scenes.summary: M3 chops vegetables with architectural precision for the lentil soup while M4 and F2 tease him affectionately.
scenes.intro: By ten o'clock Wednesday morning, bread loaves are golden in the oven and {M3} stands at the chopping board beside {F2} and {M4} with a neat row of carrots and onions. Listen first.
story: Look at {M3}'s cutting board, {F2}—every carrot cube is identical!
Even cubes cook at the exact same speed, brother. Basic physics!
Laugh all you want, {M4}, that is the neatest soup prep my kitchen has ever seen!
Pot is warm with olive oil—onions and carrots going in now?
Yes! Stir three minutes until sweet, then add red lentils and hot broth.
Need the courtyard thyme and parsley next, Chef?
Two fresh sprigs tied with string, plus one pinch of salt at the end.
Listening to soup simmer in a stone kitchen beats city traffic any day.
Funny—three years ago we argued on the phone, and today we make soup together.
Remind me never to wait three years to call you again, {M4}.
All right, brothers, save the tears—my bread timer is ringing!
Oven mitts on! Eight crusty loaves coming out hot!
scenes.outro: Golden loaves come out of the oven and fragrant lentil soup simmers on the stove as the two brothers work side by side. See you next time.

scenes.title: Setting Room Nine
scenes.summary: At half past two on Wednesday, F1, F3, and M1 lay white linen cloths, stoneware cups, and small lemon branches on the tables in Room 9.
scenes.intro: At half past two—thirty minutes before the city heritage visit—{F1}, {F3}, and {M1} put the finishing touches on the sunlit tables inside Room 9. Listen first.
story: Four white linen cloths ironed flat, three folding chairs around each table.
Look how pretty a single green leaf looks in each small glass vase, {F1}.
I hung the wooden welcome sign outside the street gate ten minutes ago.
Did anyone stop to read it on {STREET}, {M1}?
Three neighbours read every word and asked when the tea kettle boils!
Listen while I play the transition into bar twenty-eight on the piano...
Every single note rings warm and clear—especially middle D!
Leave the two arched courtyard windows open so the music carries outside.
Look at my sheet music stand: {M2}'s aunt's black ink on page one, mine on page two.
Thirty years apart, one continuous waltz.
Quarter to three on my watch. Where is {M2}?
Practising his welcome speech in the mirror—let us go rescue him!
scenes.outro: Room 9 sparkles in the afternoon sun, neighbours are already curious at the gate, and three o'clock is fifteen minutes away. See you next time.

scenes.title: Put the Speech Away
scenes.summary: At 2:55 PM, M2 nervously recites a stiff five-page history speech until F1 and M1 convince him to simply welcome the visitor naturally.
scenes.intro: Five minutes before three at the front desk, {M2} is straightening his tie and reading frantically from five sheets of paper in front of {F1} and {M1}. Let's listen in first.
story: 'Esteemed municipal representative, for over eighty years this historic courtyard...'
Boss, if you talk like a tax textbook, the clerk will fall asleep standing up.
Take one deep breath, {M2}, and put all five pages in the drawer.
In the drawer?! Then what do I say when they walk through the gate?!
Say 'Good afternoon, welcome to Room Nine, please sit down for hot tea!'
Let the sunlit glass, {F2}'s warm bread, and {F3}'s piano do the talking.
You really think simple hospitality is enough?
Hospitality is what this house has done best for over eighty years, {M2}.
Wait—are my reading glasses on my forehead right now?
Safely in your jacket pocket, boss. Tie straight, shoes clean.
Listen—the courtyard gate bell just rang! Three o'clock on the dot!
Deep breath... smile... let us go welcome our guest!
scenes.outro: The stiff speech stays in the drawer, the gate bell rings at three sharp, and {M2} steps out with a genuine smile. See you next time.

scenes.title: The Heritage Stamp
scenes.summary: After inspecting the open gate, sunlit café tables, lending books, and hot tea, the heritage clerk signs the protection form—and asks F3 to play.
scenes.intro: Twenty minutes later inside Room 9, the heritage review has checked every window, exit, book basket, and teacup—and {M2} and {F1} step over to {F3} by the piano holding a stamped white certificate! Listen first.
story: {F3}! Look at the round blue stamp at the bottom of {M2}'s page!
Approved! Official Neighbourhood Heritage Café and Guesthouse—lease protected!
Congratulations, {M2}! What did the clerk say about Room Nine?
She drank a whole cup of mint tea, ate every crumb of lemon tart, and smiled!
She said restoring a hidden ground-floor sunroom instead of building walls was genius!
And {F2} watching proudly from her cushion at the kitchen doorway saw the whole thing!
Before the clerk walked out to {STREET}, she asked if the walnut piano really works.
Play it for all of us right now, {F3}—my aunt's finished 'Courtyard Waltz'!
Open the courtyard windows wide, {F1}, so {F2} and the whole house can hear.
Windows wide open, afternoon breeze coming in—whenever you are ready, {F3}!
Listen to those first four notes floating out under our tree...
For your aunt, {M2}, and for Room Nine.
scenes.outro: The blue heritage stamp is dry on the page, the lease is safe, and 'Courtyard Waltz' floats out through the open green shutters for the first time! See you next time.

scenes.title: Toast in the Kitchen
scenes.summary: Listening to F3's piano waltz from the kitchen doorway, F2, M3, and M4 clink teacups to celebrate passing the review.
scenes.intro: At the kitchen doorway looking onto the sunlit courtyard, {F2} listens from her cushioned chair beside {M3} and {M4} as {F3}'s waltz drifts across the stones. Let's listen in first.
story: Hear how effortlessly the second half flows from the first, {M3}?
You cannot even tell where thirty years ago ends and today begins.
And not one squeak on middle D—{M1} earned two slices of lemon tart!
Raise your teacups, boys: to Room Nine and our saved courtyard!
To Chef {F2}, who ran an entire café kitchen from two pillows!
By Friday evening your ankle will be ready to greet every regular on the street.
Wait—look past the courtyard tree toward the open street gate, {M3}.
An older gentleman with a grey hat stopped right outside on the pavement.
He took his hat off when the piano reached the second page...
Wait a second—he is humming the exact melody along with {F3}!
How could a stranger on the street know an unpublished waltz from a locked room?!
Call {F1} to the gate right now—don't let him walk away!
scenes.outro: Outside the open gate, a passerby knows every note of a song locked behind a bookcase for thirty years! One last scene for Episode 5—let's listen.

scenes.title: The Tune at the Gate
scenes.summary: At the courtyard gate, M2, F1, and F3 learn the passerby was the violinist neighbor who used to play Friday duets with M2's aunt thirty years ago—and he promises to return Friday at six!
scenes.intro: {F1} hurries to the open courtyard gate with {M2} and {F3}, calling warmly to the older neighbour who stood listening on {STREET}. Listen first.
story: Excuse me, sir—would you like to come inside for a warm cup of tea?
Wait... our neighbour from the violin shop at number ten?!
Thirty years ago, he brought his violin here every Friday at six!
Wait—look at our old postcard: 'Save two chairs for the baker and the teacher'!
He was the music teacher who played Friday duets with your aunt!
He just asked me who finally finished the second half of her May waltz!
What did he say when he heard my sixteen bars through the window, {M2}?
He had tears in his eyes—he said it sounded just like her voice!
Did you invite him to our grand opening this Friday at six o'clock?!
He promised to bring his violin—and ten neighbours from down the street!
Ten extra neighbours?! {F2} is going to need twice as many lemons by Friday!
scenes.outro: The Friday duet partner from thirty years ago heard the open window and is bringing his violin—and half the street—back this Friday at six! Episode 5 is complete—see you in the Season 2 finale.
